jobs.title: Vice President – Screening Efficiency & Analytics Strategy Lead

duties: You will serve as a bridge between analytics/technology teams and operations, compliance, and governance forums, translating complex data into clear “brutal truth” narratives and decision-ready executive reporting.
Develop and maintain an enterprise metrics framework for sanctions screening, including KPI scorecards and leading/lagging indicators, with clear definitions, sources, and reporting cadence.
Establish governance standards for metric definitions, data lineage, assumptions, and auditability;
maintain documentation to support reviews/exams and change management controls.
Lead recurring stakeholder forums to present insights, drive decisions, and track benefits realization from tuning, process changes, and automation.

Analyze alert/case/disposition/investigation data to identify and quantify drivers of false positives (e.g., name commonality, geography, list updates, transliteration patterns, and data quality issues).

Deliver data-driven tuning recommendations (e.g., threshold adjustments, token/alias handling, matching logic refinements, and data standardization), including pre/post measurement and regression monitoring.
Perform structured performance reviews after watchlist updates, ruleset releases, parameter changes, and vendor upgrades;
build monitoring to detect drift, sudden spikes, or unusual match patterns and trigger investigations/corrective actions.
Recommend process control improvements (e.g., triage logic, prioritization schemes, standardization of dispositions, workload routing) with clear success metrics and benefits tracking.

Identify opportunities to automate low-risk, high-volume outcomes (e.g., repeat false positives, deterministic negative matches, smart routing, etc) and prioritize based on impact and control considerations.

Build business cases for automation (expected alert reduction, capacity released, control impacts, residual risk) and partner with technology teams to implement analytics-enabled automation (rules-based and ML-assisted).

Deliver advanced analytics capabilities (predictive modeling, segmentation, optimization, forecasting) and ensure outputs translate into operational/technology requirements with clear acceptance criteria.

Design and partner with stakeholders to deploy automated dashboards and recurring reporting tailored to operational, risk/compliance, and executive audiences (e.g., queue health/throughput, QA trends and breach alerts, strategic KPIs and cost-per-alert).

Lead condition monitoring programs for power generation and utility substation assets, establish monitoring priorities, baselines, alarm thresholds, and escalation criteria.

Monitor gas turbines, diesel and natural-gas reciprocating generators, alternators, and auxiliary equipment using vibration analysis, thermography, lubricant analysis, ultrasound, and operating trends to identify deterioration and developing faults.

assess partial-discharge data where applicable, breaker operating times and contact resistance, insulating-medium condition, and insulation test results with electrical testing specialists.

coordinate changes through approved controls.

Analyze alarms and abnormal trends, confirm data validity, assess fault severity and progression, and issue actionable recommendations with urgency, operating implications, inspection needs, and maintenance priorities.
track actions to closure and confirm equipment condition after maintenance.
Support commissioning, acceptance testing, startup and shutdown monitoring, load testing, and return-to-service activities by establishing baselines and identifying abnormal equipment behavior.
Maintain diagnostic reports, asset health dashboards, inspection records, and computerized maintenance management system data;

including practical monitoring of gas turbines and diesel and natural-gas reciprocating generators.
Demonstrated ability to perform condition monitoring of utility substation equipment
Strong practical competence in vibration data collection and analysis
and interpretation of operating and performance trends.
Advanced technical expertise in interpreting transformer dissolved gas and insulating-oil analyses
preferredSkills: Recognized vibration analyst certification at Category II or above
or machinery lubrication and oil-analysis certification.
Experience with advanced gas turbine and reciprocating-engine diagnostics
and correlation of multiple diagnostic techniques.

duties: Serve as the electrical power-generation subject-matter expert across concept development, detailed design, construction, commissioning, operational handover, and lifecycle support.

Lead design and technical reviews for grid substations, utility interconnections, high-voltage and medium-voltage substations, transformers, switchgear, breakers, protection relays, cables, grounding, metering, and communications interfaces.

Design and review MV and LV electrical distribution systems, including MV switchgear, transformers, LV switchboards, motor-control centers, panelboards, distribution boards, UPS interfaces, automatic transfer switches, and busway systems.
Review electrical interfaces for generator systems, generator step-up transformers, generator breakers, paralleling switchgear, load banks, and associated balance-of-plant electrical equipment.

Establish and validate power-system operating strategies, including utility transfer, generator paralleling, power quality monitoring, load shedding, restoration, emergency operations, and failover scenarios.
Coordinate utility-interconnection requirements, including protection coordination, relay settings, anti-islanding, transfer-trip, telemetry, metering, energization plans, and operating agreements.
Perform or review short-circuit, load-flow, arc-flash, harmonic, grounding, voltage-drop, and protective-device coordination studies.
Review electrical one-line diagrams, schematics, protection diagrams, equipment specifications, cable schedules, vendor submittals, and construction-installation packages.
Collaborate with mechanical, I&C, network, controls, construction, delivery, commissioning, and operations teams to ensure coordinated, buildable, testable, and maintainable solutions.

Develop and support commissioning plans for substation energization, equipment startup, relay testing, switchgear testing, generator testing, load-bank testing, integrated systems testing, and utility-transfer tests.
Lead root-cause analysis of electrical faults, protective trips, power-quality events, equipment failures, and recurring operational issues.
Develop electrical operating procedures, maintenance strategies, emergency-response plans, spare-parts recommendations, and lifecycle replacement plans.
